conclusion: 195 tasks matched by task_id between offline annotations and online oracle (seed_42). DEFINITIONAL NOTE: Pre-suppression binary concordance is degenerate (κ=0.0) because online is_ack is always False before the first suppression point by construction. The meaningful pre-suppression metric is 5-class function_type concordance. Pre-suppression 5-class concordance: 38.7% agreement, κ=0.176 (fair). Position 0 shows strong agreement (116/191), but later positions diverge. Post-suppression 5-class concordance: 39.5% agreement, κ=-0.027. As expected, concordance is lower after trajectory divergence. Global binary concordance (offline type==ack vs online is_ack): 57.4% agreement, κ=0.132. When offline labels a message 'acknowledgment', online agrees only 197/442 times (44.6%). Online often classifies these as 'verification' (167/442) — a systematic offline→online label shift. When online labels is_ack=True, offline agrees 197/359 times (54.9%). Overall: offline annotations provide moderate-to-fair concordance with online oracle decisions for 5-class types, with a notable systematic disagreement on the acknowledgment/verification boundary.
